Before you arrive

We ask what kind of week you have had.

A cortex reading means very little on its own. The same brain measures differently after four hours of sleep, after a double espresso, or in the third week of a hard training block. So the context is collected first, and it stays attached to the measurement for as long as you keep scanning.

What we ask about

  • Sleep, in hours and in quality
  • Caffeine, and when you last had it
  • Training and physical load
  • Illness, medication, and recent travel
  • What you personally want to understand

Sensitivity: this measure responds to sleep deprivation, caffeine intake, and task engagement.

Carried on every reading you receive

In the studio

You sit down. Nothing goes in a tube.

There is no magnet, no contrast dye, no enclosed scanner and no noise. You stay in an ordinary chair, in an ordinary room, awake and talking to a person.

Awake and upright

You are seated the whole time and can stop at any point. Nothing is injected and nothing is swallowed.

No radiation

The measurement is made with low level near infrared light, the same part of the spectrum used by a pulse oximeter on a fingertip.

Repeatable by design

Because it is quick and non invasive, it can be repeated often enough to build a line rather than a single dot.

The headset

A cap of light sources and detectors.

Pairs of emitters and detectors sit against the scalp. Each pair watches one patch of cortex beneath it. Fitting takes a few minutes and the array is placed the same way every visit, because a baseline is only worth building if the measurement is repeatable.

Source Detector Same placement each visit

While you sit there

Blood flow is the signal.

Working tissue draws oxygen. The instrument watches oxygenated blood arrive and leave across the top surface of the cortex, at millisecond and millimetre resolution.

Flying a drone over a city to spot where the traffic flows fastest and brightest.

Connectome, on how the measurement works

The working part

You are given things to do.

A resting brain tells you relatively little. You work through a set of interactive tasks on screen while the array records, so that what is captured is your cortex under load rather than your cortex idling.

How well you hold and direct focus while something competes for it.

These are the three domains your profile reports on. Each one is measured against your own previous readings, never against a population average alone.

That is the whole visit.

No recovery time, no after effects, nothing to arrange for the rest of your day. Your reading is processed and appears in your profile, and the first one quietly becomes the thing every later reading is compared against.

Your baseline

One scan is a dot.
Four is a direction.

Cortical measures move around for ordinary reasons: a short night, a heavy week, a coffee at the wrong time. Telling a real change from that everyday noise is the entire problem, and it is not solvable with a single visit. Step through the visits below and watch what your reading is actually able to say.

Visit 1

A single point

Confidence: None Stability: Unknown Quality: Good

1 data point

Why the first visit is deliberately undersold.

Plenty of things will hand you a score on the day. A score with nothing to compare it to is a number, not information. Your baseline is the reference the rest of your readings are measured against, so the first visit is worth exactly what it is: the start of the record.

1

Visit one

Your reference point is created. No change can be claimed yet.

2

Visit two

A difference appears, but it cannot yet be separated from ordinary variation.

3

Visit three

A direction becomes visible and your personal range starts to be known.

4

Visit four and beyond

Change can be stated with a confidence level attached, and set against what you were actually doing at the time.

Your brain is more plastic than blood biomarkers, for example. So people want to see every month.

Lucas Scherdel, Co Founder and CEO

What counts as a real change

A movement is only reported as meaningful when it is larger than your own measured variability, not simply different from last time. Where it is not, the reading says so.

Your own range, not a population average

Normal is defined per person. What matters is what is normal for you, and when something has meaningfully departed from it.

Signal and noise

What moves a reading, other than your brain.

These are the known sensitivities carried on every measure you receive. They are not disclaimers. They are the reason the context is collected at all, because a reading that ignores them will confidently tell you something untrue.

Known sensitivities that affect a cortical reading
FactorWhy it mattersHow it is handled
Sleep deprivationShifts how much effort a given task costs, which moves the load measure independently of any real change.Recorded at every visit and shown next to the reading.
Caffeine intakeAlters cerebral blood flow, which is the signal being measured.Timing is logged so a movement can be attributed rather than assumed.
Task engagementA distracted run measures distraction, not capacity.Flagged through the quality measure on the recording.
Time of dayOrdinary daily rhythm accounts for part of the spread in anyone's values.Comparable slots are offered for repeat visits.

What you receive

A profile, a map, and something that updates.

Your visit produces three things. Two of them arrive once. The third is the reason to come back.

A cognitive profile

Attention, cognitive load and memory, each reported with the confidence attached to it and the context it was measured in.

Your routing architecture

A map of how information actually moves across your cortex, which is individual enough to be recognisably yours.

A profile that keeps moving

Every later scan is added to the same record, so the picture gets sharper rather than starting over.

No two routing architectures look the same.

In the app

Change, with its confidence stated.

Readings are plotted against your own baseline rather than a generic scale. Where the data is thin, the interface says so instead of implying certainty it does not have.

  • Observed change, expressed as a delta from your baseline
  • A confidence level, with the number of readings behind it
  • A stability measure for how repeatable your own values are
  • A quality flag for the recording itself
  • The sensitivities that could explain a movement

Recommendations you can actually act on.

Alongside the profile you receive personalised protocol suggestions aimed at focus, memory, mental wellbeing and long term cognitive health. Because the context data sits next to the measurement, the suggestions can be tied to what was actually happening in your life rather than issued in the abstract.

How it works

Functional near infrared spectroscopy, in plain terms.

fNIRS shines low level infrared light through the scalp and reads what comes back. Oxygenated and deoxygenated blood absorb that light differently, so the returning signal reports how much oxygen a patch of cortex has just consumed. Working tissue consumes more. That is the whole principle.

Millisecond resolution

Fast enough to follow activity as it happens rather than averaging it away.

Millimetre resolution

Precise enough to distinguish neighbouring regions of the cortical surface.

Portable and quiet

No magnet and no enclosure, which is what makes frequent repeat measurement realistic.

Scope

What this measures, and what it does not.

The method reads the outer surface of the cortex. That is a real limit and it is worth being clear about before you book rather than after.

What functional near infrared spectroscopy can and cannot measure
QuestionAnswer
Which part of the brain is read?The cortex, meaning the brain's upper surface. Deeper structures are not reached by this method.
What is actually detected?Blood oxygenation change, used as a proxy for how hard that tissue is working.
Is it a diagnosis?No. The consumer studio measures performance and wellbeing indicators, not medical diagnoses.
Is it safe?Non invasive, with no radiation and no injected contrast. Light only.
Can one visit tell me if something changed?No. Change is defined against your own prior readings, which is why the programme matters more than the first appointment.
Will my result be compared to other people?Your own baseline comes first. Cohort context sits alongside it, never instead of it.

Before you come

How to give yourself a clean reading.

None of this is a rule and nothing disqualifies you from scanning. It exists because these are the things known to move the measurement, so telling us about them is what keeps your baseline honest.

Sleep

Come as you actually are, and tell us what you got. A short night is data, not a problem.

Caffeine

Keep it consistent with your normal pattern where you can, and tell us when you last had some.

Training

Note anything unusually heavy in the days before, including travel.

Timing

If you scan again, a similar time of day makes the comparison cleaner.

Who you will meet

Scanning is run by our clinical operations team. You are with a person for the whole visit, not left with a machine.

Getting here

The studio is in Soho, central London. Your confirmation email carries the exact address, the entrance to use and who to ask for.

Before you decide

Questions people ask first.

Does it hurt, and is anything injected?

Neither. The measurement is made with low level near infrared light passed through the scalp. Nothing is injected, nothing is swallowed, and there is no radiation.

How long am I actually there?

The scan itself runs twenty to thirty minutes. Add a little either side for the context questions and for fitting the array.

Will one scan tell me if something is wrong?

No, and we would rather say so plainly. A single reading has nothing to be compared against. The studio measures performance and wellbeing indicators, and it is not a diagnostic service.

How often would I come back?

Cortical measures move faster than most blood markers, so people generally want to see change on a monthly rhythm. Your reading becomes considerably more useful from the third or fourth visit onward.

What if I slept badly the night before?

Come anyway and tell us. Sleep is one of the known sensitivities, so it is recorded alongside the reading and taken into account rather than quietly distorting your baseline.

Can I bring this to my clinic or my team?

Yes. The same measurement layer runs with performance environments, clinics and research platforms. There is a separate route for organisations.
